planting.note: Set own-root plants in spring into average, well-drained soil in full sun; this Agriculture Canada rugosa hybrid needs no winter protection even on the open prairie.

directions: Jens Munk was bred by Felicitas Svejda for Agriculture Canada's Explorer series and is prized for carrying a strong rugosa constitution into a repeat-blooming, deep-pink, clove-scented shrub. Plant in full sun with sharp drainage; it tolerates poor, sandy, or saline soils and needs only light thinning of old canes in early spring to stay productive. Deadhead the earliest flush lightly to encourage rebloom, but leave the last round of flowers unpruned so the plant can set its orange-red autumn hips, which persist attractively into winter. Its extreme cold tolerance, bred for the Canadian prairies, makes it one of the hardiest repeat-blooming shrub roses available.
sources: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada — Explorer Rose Series

common_name: Charles Albanel Rugosa Rose (Explorer Series Groundcover)

planting.note: Plant in spring in full sun on well-drained soil, spacing plants to let the low, spreading canes knit together into a solid groundcover.

directions: Charles Albanel is the lowest-growing of the Explorer series rugosas, forming a dense, trailing mound rather than an upright shrub, which makes it useful as a hardy flowering groundcover or bank cover. Its magenta-pink, semi-double flowers repeat through summer and are followed by a generous crop of rounded orange-red hips that show well against the low foliage. Give it full sun and lean, well-drained soil, and prune only to remove dead wood, since heavy shearing reduces both bloom and hip set. It shares the rugged salt- and drought-tolerance of its rugosa parentage, making it a reliable choice for difficult coastal or roadside plantings.
sources: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada — Explorer Rose Series

planting.note: Install bare-root or container stock in spring in average well-drained soil; this compact rugosa hybrid is well suited to small gardens and hedging.

directions: David Thompson produces medium-red, semi-double flowers in flushes from early summer into fall, set against the crinkled, disease-resistant foliage typical of rugosa breeding. It is more compact than many rugosa hybrids, making it a practical choice for a low hedge or mixed border where a hardy shrub rose with ornamental hips is wanted. Plant in full sun with good drainage and prune lightly in early spring, removing only dead or weak canes, since the plant blooms and sets hips on growth from the current and prior season. Like its Explorer series siblings, it tolerates severe winter cold with no special protection and bears a reliable fall crop of red hips.
sources: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada — Explorer Rose Series

common_name: Henry Hudson Rugosa Rose (Explorer Series Groundcover)

planting.note: Plant in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; its low mounding habit suits foundation plantings, low hedges, or mass groundcover use.

directions: Henry Hudson opens white, clove-scented, semi-double flowers that age to a soft blush pink, held on a low, dense, mounding rugosa shrub well under three feet tall. It blooms in repeated flushes through the growing season and sets a good crop of round red hips in fall, which stand out against its typically wrinkled rugosa leaves. Site it in full sun with sharp drainage, and limit pruning to removing dead or damaged wood in early spring so both flowering and hip production are not disrupted. Bred for extreme prairie winters, it needs no mulching or wrapping even in the coldest zones where it is hardy.
sources: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada — Explorer Rose Series

planting.note: Plant own-root stock in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; this low, spreading rugosa works well as a flowering and hip-bearing groundcover or low hedge.

directions: Purple Pavement, sold in Europe as Rotes Meer, is a German-bred rugosa valued for its deep magenta-purple, semi-double flowers and compact, mounding growth habit well suited to banks and low borders. It reblooms steadily from early summer into fall and follows each flush with a heavy set of large, tomato-red hips that persist well after the leaves color up in autumn. Grow it in full sun with lean, well-drained soil, and prune only to remove old or damaged canes, since the Pavement series roses bloom and fruit best with minimal interference. It shares the rugosa family's tolerance for drought, salt spray, and difficult soils, making it a dependable landscape plant for both flowers and ornamental hips.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

planting.note: Plant in spring in full sun with sharp drainage; its low, wide habit makes it a good edging or groundcover rose where repeat bloom and fall hips are both wanted.

directions: Snow Pavement, known in Germany as Schneekoppe, bears ruffled, lavender-tinged white double flowers with a strong clove fragrance on a low, broad rugosa shrub. Repeat flushes of bloom continue through the season, and the plant sets a modest but reliable crop of rounded red hips that add fall interest once flowering slows. Plant in full sun in average to lean, well-drained soil, and limit pruning to removing dead wood in spring, since this cultivar performs best left largely alone. Like other Pavement series rugosas it tolerates drought, poor soil, and roadside salt exposure with little complaint.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

planting.note: Set plants out in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; its broader habit than other Pavement roses makes it useful as an informal low hedge.

directions: Pink Pavement carries rose-pink, semi-double, strongly fragrant flowers in repeated flushes on a mounding rugosa shrub somewhat taller than its Pavement series siblings. Spent flowers left on the plant in late summer develop into a good crop of orange-red hips that extend the shrub's season of interest into winter. Grow it in full sun with well-drained soil, water sparingly once established, and prune only to remove weak or dead canes in early spring. It combines rugosa toughness against drought and salt with a repeat-blooming, hip-bearing habit that makes it popular in low-maintenance landscape plantings.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

planting.note: Plant in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; its compact size suits small gardens, containers, or tight groundcover plantings where larger rugosas would overwhelm the space.

directions: Foxi Pavement is the most compact of the Pavement series rugosas, forming a dense, low mound rarely over two feet tall, with deep pink-magenta semi-double flowers held close to the foliage. It reblooms through summer and sets a steady supply of small, round red hips that the compact habit displays well at close range. Plant in full sun with sharp drainage, and prune only to remove dead or weak growth in early spring to preserve both flower and hip production. Its small stature and tough rugosa constitution make it one of the easier rugosa hybrids to fit into a foundation planting or small-space garden.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes
